title: Comparison of rapid solvent extraction systems for GC–MS/MS characterization of PAHs in contaminated soil
author: Haleyur, Shahsavari, et al.

steps.title: Prepare soil samples
steps.instruction: Air‑dry soil at room temperature for 1 day, sieve through a 2 mm sieve, grind with a pestle and mortar, then sieve through a 600 µm sieve and fully homogenise.

steps.title: Test PAH distribution
steps.instruction: Perform a preliminary acetone:hexane (1:1) extraction on replicate subsamples to confirm homogenous PAH distribution; verify that total PAH concentrations vary by less than 6 %.

steps.title: Weigh and condition soil
steps.instruction: For each solvent system, weigh air‑dried homogenised soil (replicates n = 3) into 50 mL screw‑cap centrifuge tubes containing 5 g pre‑dried (100 °C) sodium sulfate; hand‑shake and break any lumps with a spatula to ensure homogeneity.

steps.title: First solvent extraction
steps.instruction: Add 15 mL of the assigned solvent (hexane, dichloromethane, acetone:hexane 1:1, acetone:dichloromethane 1:1, or chloroform:methanol 2:1) to each tube, vortex briefly, shake mechanically for 10 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at 4 696 g for 5 min; transfer the supernatant to a clean 50 mL centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Second solvent extraction
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL of the same solvent to the remaining pellet, break the pellet cake with a spatula if necessary, shake for 5 min, centrifuge at 4 696 g for 5 min, transfer the supernatant and pool with the first‑extract supernatant, then adjust the combined volume to 25 mL with the appropriate solvent.

steps.title: Filter and dilute extracts
steps.instruction: Pass the pooled 25 mL extract through a 0.2 µm Teflon‑coated filter disc into a fresh 50 mL tube using a syringe, centrifuge at 4 696 g for 5 min, aliquot 50 µL into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube containing 950 µL hexane, centrifuge again at 4 696 g for 5 min, and transfer the clear supernatant to a 2 mL GC vial.

steps.title: GC‑MS/MS instrument setup
steps.instruction: Use an Agilent HP 7890B GC equipped with PAL autosampler 120 and a 10 µL syringe. Install a DB‑5 ms ultra‑inert capillary column (first column: 0.25 mm ID × 30 m × 0.25 µm; second column: 0.25 mm ID × 25 m × 0.25 µm). Inject 2 µL in pulsed splitless mode. Oven program: 50 °C (hold 1 min), ramp 25 °C min⁻¹ to 325 °C, hold 5.2 min. Carrier helium (>99.999%) flow: 1.4 mL min⁻¹ (first column) and 1.5 mL min⁻¹ (second column). Inlet temperature: 90 °C for 0.01 min, then ramp 900 °C min⁻¹ to 325 °C and hold. Transfer line 325 °C. Ion source 350 °C; quadrupole 1 and 2 at 205 °C. N₂ collision gas 1.5 mL min⁻¹, He quench gas 2.25 mL min⁻¹. Operate the Agilent 7000 c triple quadrupole MS in Multiple Reaction Monitoring (MRM) mode. Quantify each PAH by the integrated peak‑area ratio to the internal standard and identify by target ions and retention‑time order. Data acquisition with Agilent MassHunter Workstation (version B.07.01/Build 7.1.524.0).

steps.title: Statistical data analysis
steps.instruction: Report results as means of three independent measurements per solvent system. Perform one‑factor ANOVA using Minitab; if the F‑value is significant (P ≤ 0.05), apply LSD test for mean separation. Use independent‑samples t‑tests to compare extraction solvents. Present standard deviations in figures where required.
